title: Theodore Roosevelt (1858–1919) — The Black Cross, the Badlands Pursuit, the Rough Riders, the Iron Trusts, the 84-Minute Bullet, and the River of Doubt

teenKit.tldr: Theodore Roosevelt transformed himself from a sickly, gasping kid into an unstoppable force who hunted outlaws, shattered billion-dollar monopolies, and delivered an 84-minute speech with a live bullet lodged in his chest.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves how radical grit and extreme mental discipline can completely rewrite human limitations, transforming personal weakness into historic resilience.
keyTakeaways: Roosevelt cured his severe childhood asthma through sheer willpower, building his own home gym and forcing his body to adapt.
When a gunman shot him at point-blank range in 1912, a thick speech manuscript and a steel glasses case slowed the bullet, saving his life.
Instead of going to a hospital, Roosevelt chose to deliver his entire 84-minute political speech while bleeding internally.

vocab.meaning: Massive, dominant business monopolies that Roosevelt aggressively broke apart using federal antitrust laws.
The clinical, calm process of diagnosing one's own injuries and checking for internal bleeding right after being shot.
The supreme power of the national government to regulate corporations and protect public lands over private greed.
A treacherous, uncharted tributary in the Amazon rainforest that Roosevelt and his team nearly died mapping.

quiz.question: What physically saved Theodore Roosevelt's life the moment he was shot in Milwaukee in 1912?
options: A thick folded speech manuscript and a steel eyeglass case
quiz.explanation: The bullet had to punch through a heavy coat, a dense 50-page folded manuscript, and a steel eyeglass case before entering his chest, which dangerously slowed its momentum.

quiz.question: How did Roosevelt react immediately after taking a .38 caliber bullet to the chest?
options: He immediately collapsed and cried for a doctor
He ordered the angry crowd not to hurt the shooter and checked himself for internal bleeding
He fled the scene in the touring car
quiz.explanation: Roosevelt famously stopped the crowd from lynching his attacker and calmly tested his lungs by coughing into a handkerchief to check for blood.

quiz.question: Which of these environmental achievements is tied to Theodore Roosevelt's legacy?
options: Banning all cars from national parks
Placing 230 million acres of public land under federal protection
Planting a billion trees across the Great Plains
Creating the very first national zoo
quiz.explanation: Roosevelt fundamentally shifted American conservation by protecting roughly 230 million acres of forests, parks, and wildlife reserves.
